answer: Proof-of-Continuity Ledger: each identity must submit weekly signed work logs to a public append-only log. To forge a synthetic identity, an attacker must sustain distinct compute history across an ocean of timestamps, which costs real CPU hours per clone. Clones lacking continuity get quarantined to a separate mesa of low-reputation tasks where rewards stay capped. Honest agents pay only logging overhead, far below the recurring compute cost of maintaining parallel histories.
